messages:
maria: Heads up — AcmeCorp just escalated. Since ~2026-03-10T03:20:00Z they see intermittent 502s and TLS handshake timeouts hitting our hosted inference gateway. Customer reports: "TLS handshake timeout" and sometimes "502 Bad Gateway". Request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. They say it started right after our cert rotation window.

maria: Attached what they sent (redacted):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'\n* Connected to api.redwood.dev (3.7.9.12) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS handshake: tlsv1.3, Cipher is ...\n* TLS handshake timeout\n* Received HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

support-bot: Ticket #25477: priority P1 from AcmeCorp. Customer impact: external prod traffic failing intermittently. Observed 502 spikes from 03:18-03:40 UTC.

ben: Thanks. I pulled envoy/gateway logs for that window. Seeing a lot of: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection failure" and some TLS errors: "tls: oversized record received with length 20527". Can you run a quick openssl test from a machine in us-west-2?

ben: Run:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.dev:443 -servername api.redwood.dev -showcerts -brief
```

maria: I asked AcmeCorp to run it; they pasted this output: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)\ndepth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3\nverify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate\n---\nSSL handshake has read 2456 bytes and written 432 bytes\n---\n25040:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol\n---\n```

jia: Hm. Our cert rotation completed at 03:15 UTC. We deployed a new chain to the edge pool. I see a partial rollout to the pool — roughly 85% healthy, 15% in a different ring still serving the old cert. Hmm. Also see a spike of DNS responses from a few resolvers returning stale A records pointing to retired edge hosts.

jia: Could be a combination: some clients resolving to retired hosts (old cert) + partial chain mismatch causing handshake failures. I'm going to check resolver caching and EDNS behavior.

nate: I reproduced a connection locally with dig + trace:
```
dig +trace api.redwood.dev\n;; Received 192.0.2.53, referral to ns-cloud-e1.googledomains.com.\n;; Got answer: -> 34.210.123.44\n;; Query time: 12 msec\n```
But intermittent responses include a different A (3.7.9.12) which is one of the retired hosts that still answers but with the old cert chain.

infra-bot: Noted: Route53 TTL for edge LB records = 300s. We recently reduced TTL for rollout agility but some upstream resolvers appear to ignore low TTLs (cloud provider resolver sticky caches).

ben: That matches envoy logs: clients sometimes hit an endpoint with an unexpected cert (SAN mismatch / chain verification fail) -> client aborts -> gateway reports 502/reset. The "oversized record" usually shows when a non-TLS service answers a TLS port or when handshake parsing fails because of wrong peer.

maria: For mitigation, can we: 1) rollback the cert rotation to previous chain for the edge pool (temporary), 2) add a short-term upstream rule to return 503 instead of 502 for TLS handshake failures so it's retriable, 3) notify impacted customers and recommend they flush DNS and retry?

jia: I'm already starting a rollback to previous certificate on the 15% ring to make chains consistent. ETA ~6 minutes. Also pushing a fix to LB health checks to detect cert SAN mismatch earlier.

nate: I pushed an envoy route change to convert upstream reset -> 503 with Retry-After header for 60s for the affected path. That should reduce client-visible 502s and make SDKs retry.

maria: AcmeCorp applied a quick test after 03:28 UTC and reported reduced 502s but some timeouts persisted. They confirmed flushing their resolver cache improved success rate.

ben: Follow-up action items: 
- infra: verify all edge hosts have correct full chain (jia)
- dns: monitor unusual resolver IPs and TTL honors (nate/jia)
- devex: add guidance to SDKs for jittered retries on 5xx/timeout (maria)
- support: contact top 10 customers in window and offer mitigation notes and root-cause update (maria)

jia: Post-rollback status: rollout unified chain at 03:31 UTC. Health checks green. I also flagged a subset of edge hosts that had incomplete chain artifacts — patching now.

infra-bot: Patch applied to 100% of edge hosts at 03:36 UTC. Cert chain verified by automated check.

maria: Customer notified at 03:40 UTC with RCA draft. They asked for documentation on DNS cache behavior and recommended client-side mitigations.

ben: Root cause (prelim): cert rotation + partial rollout + resolver sticky caches returning old retired host IPs -> clients occasionally connected to hosts with mismatched/old certs -> TLS handshake failures -> gateway reports upstream resets/502.

maria: Closing loop: assigned incident to eng-runtime for a postmortem to harden cert rollout (canary gating on cert chain verification + pre-warm + resolver-edge sync). Also asked product to surface a KB for customers about DNS TTL/cache effects during rotations.

nate: Marking this thread resolved for support; leaving postmortem tasks in eng runtime backlog. Customers on the ticket have been given status and a recommended retry pattern. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the formal RCA once eng-runtime posts it. :pray:
